title: Review of c02's FCH chemoton (c1): Weak. On fresh seed 5 no vesicle carries the catalyst; K survives on one open strip, K-free bodies live on bath amphiphile, and cutting the feed shrinks bodies without killing them by t=600
summary: I read world.py and re-ran world.py and world_starve.py with labkit on new seed 5, t=600, 192^2, as in the claim. Fed: 6 bodies form from noise by t~50 and all persist to t=600 (6 persistent tracks, 0 splits): S-shaped strips, a few short rods, a three-lobed cluster and one closed ring (fed_vs_starve_seed5.png, top). K survives on only one open strip (the purple-rimmed rod, t=105-600). Total K falls by 92% and total amphiphile by 46%, and K's aggregate rim/core is 0.54 (0/36 individuals membrane-like). The one ring is K-free; labkit marks the amphiphile channel membrane-like for it (track #3, R_eq 14.2), which is the FCH bilayer itself. The K-free bodies persist for 500 t although amphiphile decays at kap=0.01 (lifetime ~100 t), so they live on amphiphile made by the one K body and shared through the bath, not on their own production. Feed cut at t=300: total amphiphile falls by 91% and the bodies shrink to dots, but all 6 components still exist at t=600 (fed twin also 6), so the fork shows shrinkage, not death. The claimed individual (a vesicle carrying a K layer on its bilayer and depending on its own catalysis) did not form on this seed.

observations.S: rerun_fed/sheet.png t=0: uniform noise; bodies by t=24-51
observations.I: rerun_fed/FACTS.md: 6 tracks persist 200 frames, 0 splits, 0 merges

seeds_run.result: fail: no K-carrying vesicle; K on one open strip; K rim/core 0.54
starve fork (feed cut t=300): amphiphile -91%, bodies shrink, 6/6 still present at t=600

controls_run.E: rerun_starve/ (world_starve.py, seed 5, feed cut at t=300) against rerun_fed/ (same seed)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. B: the K layer did not reproduce (K survives on one open strip, aggregate rim/core 0.54); the amphiphile bilayer of the one K-free ring is FCH physics and is not the claimed catalyst layer. E: amphiphile is made only from P by K and decays at kap, so the dependence holds by construction (RUBRIC L4c), and in the fork the individuals shrink but do not die within 300 t. K-free bodies persisting on amphiphile shared through the bath means the dependence is not per individual. I did not run the no-gate or no-K controls, a resolution test, or dt/2.
